name: tequila_scene
description: Counts, units, overall bounds and the file of the open scene.

name: tequila_nodes
description: Parts and groups: id, name, material and world size. Filter by a word in the name or material name to keep the answer short.

filter.description: Only nodes whose name or material name contains this (case-insensitive).

name: tequila_materials
description: Every material: id, type, how many parts use it, parameters and texture maps.

name: tequila_query
description: Any read-only query.

name: tequila_apply
description: Apply one command, e.g. {"command":"material.set_type","material":2,"type":"velvet"}. tequila_query what=commands lists them; what=api describes material parameters and types. One undo step. Colours may be hex sRGB strings ("value": "#c0392b"), converted for you; arrays are linear ACEScg.

name: tequila_material_guide
description: How to make procedural materials: the recipe format, every pattern kind with what it looks like and its settings and defaults, the material types, rules of thumb, and 16 tested example recipes (terrazzo, marble, brushed aluminium, walnut, carbon fibre, leather, concrete, hammered copper, galaxy resin, worn paint...). Read it before writing a recipe.

name: tequila_material_preview
description: Show a material recipe (or an existing material by id) on a ball, without changing the scene. Returns an image. The fastest way to try an idea: preview, adjust, preview again, then tequila_material_create. Recipe: {"name": "Speckled Stone", "type": "plastic" (or metal, glass, paint, velvet... see the guide), any parameter as a value ("specular_roughness": 0.3, "base_color": "#c0392b" - hex sRGB is fine), "patterns": [{"param": "base_color", "procedural": {"kind": "noise"}, "size": 0.01, "colors": [{"at": 0, "color": "#d8d4cc"}, {"at": 1, "color": "#a9a59c"}]}, {"param": "specular_roughness", "procedural": {"kind": "noise"}, "size": 0.02, "range": [0.2, 0.4]}, {"param": "bump", "procedural": {"kind": "leather"}, "size": 0.002, "depth": 0.0001}]}. `size` is the feature size in metres at real-world scale. A later pattern on the same param is a layer: "blend" mix/multiply/add, "amount" 0-1, "mask" {"threshold": 0.5, "softness": 0.05}. Pattern kinds: noise, noise_texture, ridged, cellular, spots, granite, marble, wood, wood_advanced, brushed, brushed_radial, scratches, leather, weave, camouflage, contour, mesh. Call tequila_material_guide once for what each looks like, their settings, the rules of thumb and 16 tested example recipes to start from.

radius.description: The ball's radius in metres (default 0.025). Use the real part's size to judge pattern scale.

name: tequila_material_create
description: Make a new material from a recipe and put it on parts, as one undo step. Returns its id and a preview image. Recipe: {"name": "Speckled Stone", "type": "plastic" (or metal, glass, paint, velvet... see the guide), any parameter as a value ("specular_roughness": 0.3, "base_color": "#c0392b" - hex sRGB is fine), "patterns": [{"param": "base_color", "procedural": {"kind": "noise"}, "size": 0.01, "colors": [{"at": 0, "color": "#d8d4cc"}, {"at": 1, "color": "#a9a59c"}]}, {"param": "specular_roughness", "procedural": {"kind": "noise"}, "size": 0.02, "range": [0.2, 0.4]}, {"param": "bump", "procedural": {"kind": "leather"}, "size": 0.002, "depth": 0.0001}]}. `size` is the feature size in metres at real-world scale. A later pattern on the same param is a layer: "blend" mix/multiply/add, "amount" 0-1, "mask" {"threshold": 0.5, "softness": 0.05}. Pattern kinds: noise, noise_texture, ridged, cellular, spots, granite, marble, wood, wood_advanced, brushed, brushed_radial, scratches, leather, weave, camouflage, contour, mesh. Call tequila_material_guide once for what each looks like, their settings, the rules of thumb and 16 tested example recipes to start from.

nodes.description: Part ids to put it on; the selection when left out.

preview.description: Return a preview image too (default true).

name: tequila_material_update
description: Remake an existing material from a recipe, where it is: every part using it changes. One undo step; returns a preview image. Use it to refine a material after looking at it on the product. Recipe: {"name": "Speckled Stone", "type": "plastic" (or metal, glass, paint, velvet... see the guide), any parameter as a value ("specular_roughness": 0.3, "base_color": "#c0392b" - hex sRGB is fine), "patterns": [{"param": "base_color", "procedural": {"kind": "noise"}, "size": 0.01, "colors": [{"at": 0, "color": "#d8d4cc"}, {"at": 1, "color": "#a9a59c"}]}, {"param": "specular_roughness", "procedural": {"kind": "noise"}, "size": 0.02, "range": [0.2, 0.4]}, {"param": "bump", "procedural": {"kind": "leather"}, "size": 0.002, "depth": 0.0001}]}. `size` is the feature size in metres at real-world scale. A later pattern on the same param is a layer: "blend" mix/multiply/add, "amount" 0-1, "mask" {"threshold": 0.5, "softness": 0.05}. Pattern kinds: noise, noise_texture, ridged, cellular, spots, granite, marble, wood, wood_advanced, brushed, brushed_radial, scratches, leather, weave, camouflage, contour, mesh. Call tequila_material_guide once for what each looks like, their settings, the rules of thumb and 16 tested example recipes to start from.

recipe.description: The new recipe. Without a name the material keeps its own.

preview.description: Return a preview image too (default true).

name: tequila_material_recipe
description: Read any material - one you made, or a library preset already on a part - back as a recipe, to change it and send it to tequila_material_update or tequila_material_create.

name: tequila_material_save
description: Keep a material in the person's own material library, so it is in the Library tab for every project.

name: tequila_batch
description: Several operations as ONE undo step. Each is a request object with an "op": apply, select, frame, look, ui, import, save, screenshot, queue. If one fails the whole batch is taken back, unless atomic is false.

name: tequila_undo
description: Take back the last step (a single edit or a whole batch).

name: tequila_redo
description: Put back the last undone step.

name: tequila_select
description: Replace the selection with these node ids.

name: tequila_frame
description: Point the camera at everything, or at the selection.

all.description: true for everything (default), false for the selection.

name: tequila_look
description: Place the camera: a standard view, orbit angles around a target, or an exact eye position. Undoable.

from.description: Eye position [x, y, z]; not with yaw/pitch/distance.

yaw.description: Degrees around +Y; 0 looks from the front.

name: tequila_screenshot
description: See the application as it is now. Returns an image.

viewport.description: true for just the 3D view, without panels (default true).

name: tequila_render
description: Render the current view to an image and return it. Blocks Tequila while it runs: keep it small (e.g. 640x400, 32 samples).

name: tequila_queue
description: Start a background render with the document's render settings; returns a job id at once. Poll tequila_jobs. studio renders one view; studios=true renders every view.

studio.description: A Studio (a view) by name or index, applied for the render and taken back.

studios.description: Every Studio, one render each, named for its view.

name: tequila_jobs
description: The background render queue: state, progress and output file of each job.

name: tequila_studio_presets
description: The studio presets installed: complete studios - lights, cameras and views, floor, look - for a kind of product, by family and size. Each lists its views and the product radius it was framed for; "suggested" marks the size in each family nearest the product in the scene.

name: tequila_studio_preset_apply
description: Apply an installed studio preset as ONE undo step: its lights, cameras and views (Studios), environment and floor, look and render settings, framed to the product's size and the product stood on its floor. The first view is applied; tequila_studio_render_all renders them all.

front.description: The product's side that should face the Main camera (default +z).

scale.description: What follows the product's size (default: the preset's own choice).

keep_placement.description: Leave the product where it is.

dress.description: Also put the preset's materials on parts by their names (its material rules).

name: tequila_studio_preset_save
description: Keep the scene's studio - everything but the product - as a studio preset of the person's own, framed for the product it has now.

materials.description: Keep the project's materials with it.

name: tequila_studio_render_all
description: Render every view (Studio) in the background, one image each, named for its view. Only when asked for renders.

name: tequila_stop
description: Stop the running background render; it still writes its image.

name: tequila_ui
description: Open or close panels and switch the viewport shading.

graph.description: Open the Material Graph editor on this material number; false closes it.

name: tequila_import
description: Load a model file into the scene: STEP or IGES (CAD, divided into parts with their colours), glTF/GLB, OBJ, STL, USD (.usda) or IFC. Not FBX: ask for glTF, OBJ or USD instead.

name: tequila_save
description: Save the project, to its own file or to a new path.

name: tequila_plugin_guide
description: How to write a Tequila plugin: the full reference (manifest, Python API, panels and their field types, events, material packs), a working template, and the way to work - write, ask the person to turn it on, run, read the log, fix. Read it once before writing a plugin.

name: tequila_plugin_list
description: Every installed plugin: id, name, version, whether it is on, running or failed (and why), its commands, panels and events, and its folder. Also whether Python was found, and the person's plugins folder.

name: tequila_plugin_write
description: Write a plugin's files into the person's plugins folder: a new plugin, or new versions of an existing one's files (others are kept). Give plugin.json (its id must be `id`) and main.py at least for a new one. Text files only (.py .json .md .txt .csv .toml .ini .cfg), paths inside the plugin's folder. A running plugin restarts with the new code; a new one must be turned on with tequila_plugin_enable.

id.description: The plugin id and folder name, e.g. "my.batch-renamer": letters, digits, . - _

files.description: Path inside the plugin folder -> the file's full text, e.g. {"plugin.json": "...", "main.py": "..."}.

name: tequila_plugin_enable
description: Turn a plugin on. A plugin with Python code runs as the person, so Tequila asks them in its Plugins window and only they can say yes: tell them to look at Tequila, then check tequila_plugin_list for "enabled". A material pack is turned on at once.

name: tequila_plugin_run
description: Run one of an enabled plugin's commands (or a panel button's command) with `values` as its panel would send them, wait a little, and return what it logged: its prints, status messages, `finished`, or the traceback if it failed. A command with a panel opens the panel instead.

values.description: Field id -> value, as the panel would send.

wait.description: Seconds to wait for it to finish (default 10, at most 120).

name: tequila_plugin_log
description: The last lines of a plugin's log: what it printed, its status messages, finished commands and tracebacks. Use it to debug.

name: tequila_request
description: Send any raw request object (with an "op") for anything the other tools do not cover.
